data.narrative:
Saltfoss Energy is a Series A nuclear energy company that has raised $40M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 11 peers spanning the nuclear sector: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private firms including Valar Atomics, Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, and X-Energy at overlapping or adjacent stages.

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression modeling uses the $40M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A to subsequent funding rounds, implying $80M. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector comparables—Valar Atomics at $6.0B (Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy at $808M (Seed), and Fuse Energy at $200M (Series A)—yields a median valuation of $808M, with a range spanning $200M to $6.0B. The wide peer dispersion reflects stage variance and heterogeneous commercial maturity within the nuclear sector.

Triangulating these methods produces a valuation range of $68M (low) to $929M (high), with a median of $444M. The $861M spread reflects meaningful uncertainty around Saltfoss's technical readiness, capital efficiency relative to peer benchmarks, and sector-wide commercialization timelines. Stage-progression and peer-median estimates diverge substantially, suggesting that comparable-company selection and stage alignment are critical sensitivities. Further clarity on engineering milestones and capital requirements would narrow this range.
